# CODON-TOPO

> Computational pipeline validating the algebraic structure of genetic codes when encoded as 6-bit binary vectors in GF(2)^6, across all 27 NCBI translation tables. Accompanies Clayworth & Kornilov, *BioSystems* (in press).

The paper's central claim is that the standard genetic code is unusually low-cost across four physicochemical distance metrics under a quartet-pattern shuffle null (see §NULL of the corrections ledger for the naming history and the classical Haig–Hurst amino-acid-permutation companion), that natural codon reassignments are depleted for topology-breaking moves (moves that fragment an amino-acid codon family under H(3, 4) single-nucleotide adjacency), and that conditional-logit modelling of event-level reassignments shows physicochemical smoothness and codon-family topology contribute independently. Five secondary results (tRNA-gene enrichment, bit-position bias, mechanism boundary cases, Atchley F3/Serine convergence, and a disconnection catalogue) are reported as exploratory. Four algebraic conjectures previously associated with this project (Serine min-distance-4 invariant, PSL(2,7) as a symmetry group, a holomorphic GF(2)^6 → C^3 embedding, and a KRAS–Fano clinical prediction) were tested and are recorded as rejected or falsified.

## Getting started

- [README](README.md) — install, headline results, one-command reproduction
- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) — release notes; v0.6.1 is the consolidated pre-publication QA/QC release (null-model description math, MC tail convention, tRNA-vector reconciliation against primary literature, and H(3,4) clade-exclusion table)
- [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) — machine-readable citation, cite the paper and this repository together
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) — repository conventions and constraints (R + ggplot2 for figures, 27 NCBI translation tables, quartet-pattern shuffle null at n = 10,000, etc.)

## Source layout

- [Core computation](src/codon_topo/core/) — GF(2)^6 encoding, 27 NCBI translation tables, filtration primitives, persistent-homology on codon graphs, XOR-triple (Fano) computation, coordinate-wise root-of-unity embedding
- [Analysis modules](src/codon_topo/analysis/) — quartet-pattern shuffle + classical Haig–Hurst AA-permutation nulls, reassignment database, depth calibration, hypercube coloring optimality, tRNA repertoire evidence (Fisher–Stouffer + Bron–Kerbosch MIS enumeration + topology-breaking subset), synthetic-biology structural-preservation index, conditional-logit models
- [Reports](src/codon_topo/reports/claim_hierarchy.py) — the single source of truth for the paper's 15 claims and their status (Supported / Exploratory / Rejected / Falsified / Tautological)
- [Visualization](src/codon_topo/visualization/R/) — R + ggplot2 scripts that regenerate every published figure from the pipeline JSONs
- [Command-line interface](src/codon_topo/cli.py) — `codon-topo all --output-dir=./output --seed=135325 --n=10000` regenerates every published statistic and writes a consolidated `manuscript_stats.json` for the Typst manuscript

## Manuscript sources

- [output/manuscript.pdf](output/manuscript.pdf) — main manuscript, compiled via Typst 0.14.2 from `output/manuscript.typ`
- [output/supplement.pdf](output/supplement.pdf) — supplement (S1–S24), compiled from `output/supplement.typ`
- [output/references.bib](output/references.bib) — bibliography with BibTeX-safe diacritics
- [docs/publisher/](docs/publisher/) — per-item corrections ledger with commit-hash provenance
- [output/publisher_letter.pdf](output/publisher_letter.pdf) — cover letter to the *BioSystems* production editor

## Data and reproducibility

- [data/assembly_accessions.tsv](data/assembly_accessions.tsv) — 18 NCBI genome assemblies used for the tRNAscan-SE 2.0.12 uniform re-scan
- [data/trnascan_results/](data/trnascan_results/) — raw `.out` and `.stats` files from tRNAscan-SE
- [scripts/run_trnascan.sh](scripts/run_trnascan.sh) — reproduces every scan from the accession list
- [scripts/generate_tables.py](scripts/generate_tables.py) — regenerates the T-CSV files under `output/tables/` from the pipeline JSONs
- Random seed: `135325` across every Monte Carlo path; every generated PDF, JSON, and figure is bit-reproducible given the same seed and the same tRNAscan-SE 2.0.12 raw outputs

## Optional

- [Tests](tests/) — 400+ pytest tests including the full PRD Appendix 8 regression (`tests/test_regression.py`), Hypothesis property tests, and CLI smoke tests
- [Scripts](scripts/) — auxiliary utilities (Walsh spectrum, Slavov SAAP, conditional-logit diagnostics)
